title: AIVector MS-DOS Asteroids clone release
author: Playful-Whole7859
selftext:
I have created an Asteroids clone for MS-DOS using DJGPP and Allegro 4.2. I wanted to find out if a local LLM running on modest mid range gaming hardware with the right instructions and documentation could write good, well optimized code in a somewhat less familiar language for an outdated platform, all things which should be less prominent in the training data of a modern LLM.

Turns out it can, but requires a fair bit of human oversight from someone who knows the tricks of the era. I have released it open source. The downloadable build runs on a well set up fast 486 DX2-66 with a good VLB graphics card on normal details. High detail was tested on a 133Mhz AM5x86. DOSBox on a modern computer obviously runs it well too.

Game download on itch: [https://wolfbayne.itch.io/aivector](https://wolfbayne.itch.io/aivector)  
More technical info and source on git: [https://github.com/Wolfbayne77/AIVector](https://github.com/Wolfbayne77/AIVector)

comments.author: Playful-Whole7859
comments.body:
Why?  
I wanted to know if LLMs could go outside of its comfort zone, this could be important for maintaining old industrial automation machinery, PLC systems, or any number of old legacy machinery or medical equipment for example, running archaic code in extinct languages. And it may not always be acceptable to upload said code to the public Internet, so you'd have to use a local LLM. I went with MS-DOS and the 486 because Iäm very familiar with them, and GCC89 is far enough out of normal LLM training to need some specialist treatment, and the 486 platform is restrictive enough in performance that the generated code would actually have to be pretty tight and well written.

I wanted to share the result as is, so other people might check the code out and see that yes, it can absolutely be done, but it requires very specific and restrictive instructions, and RAG documentation for the platform in question.
